objectives: Translate a verbal problem into sets, logic, recurrences, finite-state machines, or graphs.

glossary: A declarative statement that is either true or false.
A statement containing variables; it becomes a proposition when variables are assigned or quantified.
A function that is both one-to-one and onto; it proves two finite sets have equal size.
An equation that defines sequence terms from earlier terms, together with base cases.
A formal power series whose coefficients encode a sequence.
An alphabet is a finite symbol set; a language is any set of finite strings over it.
A finite set of states and transitions used to recognize strings or model reactive behavior.
A walk may repeat vertices and edges; a trail does not repeat edges; a path does not repeat vertices.
A maximal set of vertices mutually reachable by paths.
A tree containing every vertex of a connected graph.
A set of edges with no common endpoint.
A flow-network view showing where existing flow can be increased, decreased, or rerouted.
A property preserved during an operation or algorithm and used to prove correctness.
types: Counting rules
Sum rule; product rule; complement counting; pigeonhole principle; inclusion-exclusion.
Use the rule that matches whether choices are exclusive, sequential, easier through a complement, forced to collide, or overlapping.
Logic forms
Proposition, predicate, tautology, contradiction, implication, equivalence, quantification.
Truth tables suit finite propositional forms; quantified claims require a domain and careful negation.
Set operations
Union, intersection, difference, complement, Cartesian product, power set.
The operation determines whether elements are pooled, shared, removed, paired, or collected as subsets.
Recurrences
Linear/nonlinear; homogeneous/non-homogeneous; constant/variable coefficients; first/higher order.
Classification determines which solution techniques apply; base cases remain essential.
Finite-state machines
Deterministic and nondeterministic finite automata.
A DFA has exactly one transition per state-symbol pair; an NFA may have several or none, yet both recognize regular languages.
Graphs
Undirected/directed; simple/multigraph; weighted/unweighted; connected/disconnected; cyclic/acyclic; bipartite.
Choose a model from relationship direction, repeated links, costs, reachability, cycles, and vertex roles.
Traversal
Breadth-first and depth-first search.
BFS explores distance layers; DFS follows a branch deeply before backtracking.
Optimization structures
Shortest path, minimum spanning tree, matching, assignment, maximum flow.
They optimize different objects: a route, a connecting subgraph, disjoint pairs, one-to-one allocation, or transported quantity.
formulas: At least one of k boxes receives this many of n objects.
Check degrees in an undirected graph.
Characterize a finite tree alongside connectedness or acyclicity.
Count undirected edges among n distinct vertices.
Ensure a flow does not exceed an edge capacity.
Required at every non-source, non-sink vertex.

comparisons.title: Eulerian versus Hamiltonian

comparisons.title: MST versus shortest-path tree

pitfalls: Negating 'for every' as 'for no' instead of 'there exists a counterexample'.
Applying the product rule where cases overlap or are mutually exclusive.
Writing a recurrence without enough base cases.
Treating a directed edge as symmetric.
Calling every sequence of adjacent vertices a path even when vertices repeat.
Using Dijkstra when negative edge weights are allowed.
Assuming a minimum spanning tree minimizes every pairwise route.
Forgetting reverse residual edges while augmenting a flow.
practice: Use inclusion-exclusion to count integers from 1 to 100 divisible by 2 or 5.
Count each set, subtract their intersection (multiples of 10).
Negate: Every server responds or at least one backup is active.
Apply De Morgan's laws and switch universal to existential where required.
Build a DFA for binary strings containing an even number of 1s.
Use two states representing parity and toggle on input 1.
Prove that a tree with n vertices has n-1 edges.
Use induction by removing a leaf.
Trace BFS and DFS from the same start vertex and record discovery edges.
Fix an adjacency order because valid traversals need not be unique.
Decide whether a degree sequence can have an Euler circuit.
Check connectedness of non-isolated vertices and degree parity.
Run one iteration of Kruskal on a weighted graph.
Sort edges and reject any edge that closes a cycle.
Find an augmenting path and update residual capacities.
The increase equals the smallest residual capacity on the path.

Represent buildings as vertices and walkways as weighted edges. Compare a shortest emergency route with a minimum-cost network connecting every building.
Job allocation model
Construct a bipartite graph of candidates and jobs, attach suitability costs, and explain how matching constraints prevent duplicate assignment.
Protocol state model
Design a finite-state machine for login attempts, success, lockout, and reset; list accepted and rejected event sequences.

Reduction of signal strength during propagation.
Mapping information onto a carrier by varying amplitude, frequency, phase, or a combination.
Elapsed time for data to travel from source to destination, including processing, queueing, transmission, and propagation.

types: Transmission media
Twisted pair, coaxial cable, optical fiber, terrestrial radio, microwave, satellite.
Guided media constrain the signal path; wireless media enable mobility but face shared-spectrum and propagation effects.
Transmission direction
Simplex, half-duplex, full-duplex.
Only one direction; alternating directions; or simultaneous directions.
Modulation families
ASK, FSK, PSK, QAM.
They vary amplitude, frequency, phase, or amplitude-plus-phase; higher symbol density demands better signal quality.
Error control
Parity, checksum, CRC, forward-error correction, retransmission protocols.
Detection identifies likely corruption; correction recovers data directly or requests another copy.
Topologies
Bus, star, ring, mesh, tree, hybrid.
They differ in path redundancy, wiring, fault effects, expansion, and management.
Internetworking devices
Repeater, hub, bridge, switch, router, gateway, proxy.
Their forwarding scope ranges from raw signals to frames, packets, and application-specific translation.
Security services
Confidentiality, integrity, authentication, authorization, availability, accountability.
Each addresses a different threat; encryption alone does not supply all services.
Network management
Configuration, fault, performance, security, and accounting management.
The categories organize what must be controlled, diagnosed, measured, protected, and attributed.
SNMP operations
Get, GetNext/GetBulk, Set, Response, Trap/Inform.
Polling reads data, Set changes permitted objects, and notifications report events.
Management interfaces
CLI, desktop tools, web interfaces, APIs, XML-based structured exchange.
They differ in automation, usability, consistency, and security surface.
formulas: Upper bound for a noisy channel under model assumptions.
Ideal noiseless band-limited channel with M signal levels.

Time for a signal front to travel through the medium.

Define topology, messages, controlled variable, timestamps, repeated trials, and plots.

objectives: Construct probability models and verify their assumptions.
Choose a distribution from the data-generating story rather than visual resemblance alone.
Simulate random variables and quantify Monte Carlo uncertainty.
Estimate parameters and interpret confidence intervals correctly.
Select, check, and communicate a statistical model or hypothesis test.
glossary: One possible result of a random experiment.
A set of outcomes from a sample space.
Probability restricted to cases where a conditioning event occurred.
A property where joint probability factorizes into marginal probabilities.
Mass for discrete values; density for continuous values; cumulative probability up to a value.
A probability-weighted long-run average of a random variable.
Expected squared deviation from the mean.
A collection of random variables indexed by time or another ordered set.
A rule computed from sample data to infer an unknown parameter.
Estimated standard deviation of a statistic's sampling distribution.
A procedure that captures the target parameter at a stated long-run rate under its assumptions.
Under the null model, the probability of a result at least as incompatible as the observed result by the chosen statistic.
Probability of rejecting the null for a specified alternative when that alternative is true.
Observed response minus fitted response in a statistical model.
types: Event relations
Mutually exclusive, exhaustive, complementary, independent, conditionally independent.
Mutual exclusion concerns overlap; independence concerns probability factorization and they are generally not the same.
Discrete distributions
Bernoulli, Binomial, Geometric, Negative Binomial, Poisson.
They model one trial, successes in fixed trials, waiting for first or r-th success, or event counts.
Continuous distributions
Exponential, Gamma, Weibull, Hyperexponential, Normal.
They model waiting time, positive duration with shape flexibility, mixtures, or symmetric additive variation.
Processes
Bernoulli process, Poisson process, discrete-time Markov chain, queueing process.
They differ by time scale, state, dependence, and event/service structure.
Sampling statistics
Sample mean, proportion, variance, regression coefficient, test statistic.
Each has a sampling distribution used for uncertainty quantification.
Estimators
Method of moments, maximum likelihood, interval estimation.
Moment matching is direct; likelihood optimization uses the full specified probability model; intervals express uncertainty.
Tests
One- or two-sided; parametric or nonparametric; association, mean, proportion, regression, or ANOVA tests.
Choice follows the question, design, measurement scale, dependence, and assumptions.
Regression models
Simple linear, multiple linear, logistic.
Linear regression targets a numeric conditional mean; logistic regression targets binary-event log-odds.
Robust/nonparametric methods
Robust summaries and estimators; rank-, sign-, permutation-, or resampling-based procedures.
They reduce sensitivity to outliers or distributional assumptions but still have assumptions.
Anomalies
Point, contextual, and collective anomalies.
Unusualness may concern one observation, its context, or a group pattern.
formulas: Reverse conditioning using prior and evidence.
Exactly k successes in n independent equal-probability trials.
Count events with mean rate parameter lambda under model assumptions.
E[X]=sum x p(x) or integral x f(x) dx
Use in normal/CLT reasoning when conditions hold.
Estimate a population mean with stated confidence procedure.
Compare observed and expected categorical counts.
Relate average number, arrival rate, and average time in a stable system.

Interpreting a 95% confidence interval as a 95% probability statement about a fixed parameter after observation.
Equating statistical significance with practical importance.
Failing to account for repeated testing.
Fitting regression without inspecting residuals, influence, or leakage.
Calling an unusual value erroneous without contextual evidence.

Diagnose a regression from residual plots.
Look for curvature, unequal spread, outliers, dependence, and influential points.
Compare bootstrap and Monte Carlo simulation.
Bootstrap resamples observed data; Monte Carlo samples from a specified model.
Choose an anomaly threshold.
Use baseline variation and costs of false positives versus false negatives.

Experiment analysis
Plan sample summaries, confidence intervals, effect size, hypothesis test, assumption checks, and a clear limitation statement.
Reliability study

objectives: Formulate a learning task with data, representation, target, loss, and evaluation protocol.

glossary: A measurable representation supplied to a learning algorithm.
Observed target value used in supervised learning.
The set of functions a learning algorithm may choose from.
A numeric penalty measuring prediction error for an example.
Performance on relevant unseen data from the target setting.
A prior represents assumptions before data; a likelihood scores observed data under parameter values.
A data summary retaining all model-relevant information about a parameter.
A measure of decision-boundary separation used by support vector machines.
A similarity function enabling implicit feature-space computation when its mathematical conditions hold.
A directed acyclic graph representing a factorization of a joint distribution.
A contiguous sequence of n items used to model local context.
An unobserved state inferred from emitted observations in a latent-state model.
A capacity measure based on the largest point set a class can shatter.
A group produced from an explicit similarity, distance, or probabilistic criterion.
Information from validation, test, or future data improperly influencing training.
types: Learning outputs
Classifiers, functions, relations, grammars, probabilistic models, value functions, behaviors, programs.
The required output structure determines representation, loss, and evaluation.
Learning settings
Supervised, unsupervised, semi-supervised, reinforcement-style behavioral learning.
They differ in feedback: labels, no labels, partial labels, or reward/interaction.
Inference principles
Bayesian posterior, maximum a posteriori, maximum likelihood, minimum description length.
They differ in treatment of priors, probability, and complexity.
Classifier families
Decision tree, neural network, SVM, Bayesian network, nearest neighbour, ensemble.
They offer different inductive biases, optimization, interpretability, and data requirements.
Text representations
Bag of words, n-grams, probabilistic sequences.
They progressively retain counts, short order, or structured dependence.
Sequence models
Markov model and hidden Markov model.
Markov states are observed in the basic model; HMM states are latent and emit observations.
Ensembles
Bagging, boosting, voting/averaging.
Bagging reduces variance through resampling; boosting builds sequentially around errors; voting combines outputs.
Reduction methods
Feature selection and feature extraction/dimensionality reduction.
Selection keeps original variables; extraction creates new lower-dimensional coordinates.
Clustering
Partitioning, hierarchical, model-based, distributional.
They differ in output structure and definition of cluster membership.
Evaluation
Holdout, cross-validation, confusion-matrix metrics, calibration, error analysis.
The protocol must match deployment population and prevent leakage.
formulas: Measure uncertainty; used in tree splitting and information theory.
Classify relative to a learned hyperplane.
majority or weighted vote among k nearest samples
Approximate sequence probability with limited context.
Choose class with greatest posterior proportional score.
required samples rise with capacity and desired confidence
Reason about generalization rather than memorize one bound.
maximize projected variance subject to orthonormal directions
Fraction of predicted positives that are correct.
Harmonic summary of precision and recall.

objectives: Turn a broad topic into a feasible research problem, question, and testable hypothesis.
Choose a qualitative, quantitative, or mixed design that supports the intended inference.
Define constructs and measurements with evidence for validity and reliability.
Select and document a sampling strategy and analysis plan.
Write, cite, and publish research ethically with a reproducible evidence trail.
glossary: A defensible gap, uncertainty, contradiction, or practical need that motivates systematic inquiry.
A specific answerable question defining population or context, concepts, and intended relationship or description.
An organized explanation connecting concepts and expected relationships.
An abstract idea such as usability, trust, or learning that requires operational definition.
A measured representation that can take different values.
The exact procedure used to observe, classify, or calculate a concept.
A specific testable expectation linked to variables and a population or context.
Evidence supporting the interpretation and use of a measurement or inference.
Consistency of measurement under defined conditions.
The operational source or list from which sample units are selected.
Random difference between a sample estimate and population value caused by observing a sample.
Missing participation or measurements from selected units, potentially creating bias.
Comparison or integration of multiple methods, sources, investigators, or theories.
Presenting another's words, ideas, or work without appropriate attribution.
Misleading reuse of one's prior text or results without transparent disclosure or citation.
types: Reasoning
Deductive and inductive.
Deduction derives testable expectations from theory; induction develops patterns or theory from observations.
Research purpose
Exploratory, descriptive, explanatory/experimental.
Explore an unclear problem, describe a phenomenon, or test an effect/relationship under a design.
Approach
Qualitative, quantitative, mixed methods.
They prioritize contextual meaning, numerical measurement, or planned integration of both.
Variables
Independent, dependent, control, confounding, mediator, moderator.
Their role concerns presumed cause/input, outcome, held conditions, alternative explanation, mechanism, or changing effect.
Validity evidence
Construct, content, criterion-related, internal, external.
The relevant validity question depends on whether concern is measurement meaning, coverage, agreement, causal inference, or generalization.
Reliability
Test-retest, inter-rater, internal consistency, equivalent-form.
They assess stability over time, agreement, coherence among items, or agreement across forms.
Measurement levels
Nominal, ordinal, interval, ratio.
They allow category, order, equal differences, and finally meaningful ratios from a true zero.
Probability sampling
Simple random, systematic, stratified random, multistage.
They select individuals directly, by interval, within strata, or across staged clusters/units.
Non-probability sampling
Convenience, purposive, quota, snowball.
Selection probabilities are unknown; these may fit exploratory access needs but constrain population inference.
Analysis
Univariate and bivariate in the supplied syllabus.
Univariate summarizes one variable; bivariate examines association or comparison between two.
Research communication
Dissertation/thesis-style report, research paper, review article, short communication, conference presentation.
Formats differ in scope, novelty, depth, audience, and length; venue rules govern the final structure.
Source tools
Encyclopedias, research guides, handbooks, academic databases.
Use orientation sources to learn vocabulary and databases to discover and trace research literature.
formulas: Audit whether every stage supports the intended claim.
Reason about reliability and measurement quality.
Describe the share of a finite population selected.

row total x column total / grand total
